momo.name: Momo
momo.description: Steamed or fried bite-sized dumplings filled with minced meat (buff, chicken, pork) or finely shredded vegetables, seasoned with aromatic Himalayan spices.
momo.cultural_significance: Undoubtedly Nepal's unofficial national comfort dish and most popular culinary export, cherished across generations and gatherings.
momo.recipe_summary: Roll thin dough circles, fill with spiced stuffing, pleat into crescent or pouch shapes, and steam in a layered steamer for 10-12 minutes.
momo.suggested_accompaniments: Served piping hot with fiery tomato-sesame achar and roasted timur (Sichuan pepper) dip.

selroti.name: Selroti
selroti.description: Ring-shaped traditional Nepali sweet fried rice bread with a crispy exterior and soft, airy crumb.
selroti.cultural_significance: Indispensable symbol of festive celebrations including Dashain, Tihar, wedding rituals, and ceremonial pujas.
selroti.recipe_summary: Semi-liquid rice batter is beaten until fluffy, then hand-poured in circular rings into smoking-hot ghee or oil and flipped with wooden sticks until golden brown.
selroti.suggested_accompaniments: Freshly brewed masala milk tea (Chiya), spicy aloo achar, or sukuti.

dalbhat.name: Dal Bhat Tarkari
dalbhat.description: The quintessence of daily Nepali life: steamed white or brown rice (Bhat) served alongside slow-cooked lentil soup (Dal) and seasonal spiced vegetables (Tarkari).
dalbhat.cultural_significance: Consumed twice daily by millions, captured by the beloved mountaineering phrase 'Dal Bhat Power 24 Hour'.
dalbhat.recipe_summary: Lentils are boiled and tempered (chhonk) with ghee, garlic, and jimbu. Accompanied by pan-sautéed vegetable curry, fresh greens (Saag), and tomato chutney.
dalbhat.suggested_accompaniments: Fermented radish pickle (Mula ko Achar), fried sun-dried papad, and fresh sliced lemons.

panipuri.name: Panipuri
panipuri.origin: Pan-South Asian street culture with iconic Nepali spicy-tangy twists
panipuri.description: Crisp, hollow fried semolina dough balls (puris) punctured and stuffed with mashed spiced potatoes, chickpeas, and plunged into ice-cold tart herbal mint-tamarind water.
panipuri.cultural_significance: Beloved social street ritual across Kathmandu, Pokhara, and town squares throughout Nepal.
panipuri.recipe_summary: Hollow sphere is lightly crushed on top, spooned with seasoned potato filling, immersed in zesty herbal water, and eaten whole in one bite.

samosa.name: Samosa & Tarkari
samosa.origin: Terai & Pahad tea stalls across Nepal
samosa.description: Flaky, crisp pyramid pastries filled with tempered diced potatoes, green peas, and whole cumin, commonly served topped with savory chickpea curry (Tarkari).
samosa.cultural_significance: The most widely enjoyed morning and afternoon tea-time companion across roadside tea stalls in Nepal.
samosa.recipe_summary: Crisp flour pastry is folded into neat cones, stuffed with spiced potato mixture, sealed, and deep-fried at gentle temperatures until golden amber.
samosa.suggested_accompaniments: Hot chana tarkari (chickpea gravy) with sweet-tangy tamarind chutney.

chiya.name: Masala Chiya
chiya.description: Rich, aromatic spiced milk tea brewed with full-bodied local CTC tea leaves (Ilam), fresh milk, and fragrant whole spices.
chiya.cultural_significance: The heart of Nepali hospitality and social culture; no guest enters a home without being greeted with a steaming glass of Chiya.
chiya.recipe_summary: Water and milk are brought to a roll with crushed spices and ginger, black tea is added and slow-boiled until deep amber, strained into glasses.
chiya.suggested_accompaniments: Paired with morning Selroti, bakery biscuits, or Malpuwa.

pakauda.name: Pakauda
pakauda.origin: Pan-Nepal roadside tea shops & household rainy-day tradition
pakauda.description: Crunchy, golden-brown deep-fried fritters made by dipping sliced onions, potatoes, cabbage, or paneer into spiced chickpea flour (besan) batter.
pakauda.cultural_significance: The perennial companion to a rainy afternoon or roadside evening tea break across Nepal.
pakauda.recipe_summary: Coarsely mixed vegetable and seasoned besan batter is spooned in bite-sized clumps into hot mustard oil and deep-fried until crisp and golden brown.
pakauda.suggested_accompaniments: Fiery tomato-coriander chutney and steaming hot glass of Masala Chiya.

jeri.name: Jeri (Jalebi)
jeri.origin: Historic sweetmakers of Kathmandu Valley & Pan-Nepal
jeri.description: Crisp, spiraled pretzel-shaped fried batter soaked in aromatic cardamom and saffron-infused warm sugar syrup.
jeri.cultural_significance: Celebratory morning staple; famously folded inside warm soft Swari bread ('Jeri-Swari') for auspicious festival breakfasts in Kathmandu.
jeri.recipe_summary: Fermented batter is poured through a cloth nozzle into hot ghee in concentric spiral coils, fried until crisp, then soaked in warm aromatic sugar syrup.
jeri.suggested_accompaniments: Warm Swari flatbread or fresh thick curd (Dahi).

yomari.name: Yomari
yomari.description: Fig-shaped steamed rice flour dumpling filled with sweet molten molasses (Chaku) and sesame seeds, or savory lentil paste.
yomari.cultural_significance: Centerpiece of Yomari Punhi, celebrating the post-harvest full moon and bestowing prosperity and blessings upon families.
yomari.recipe_summary: Warm dough is sculpted with fingers into pointed conical figures, hollowed out, packed with warm chaku-sesame filling, pinched closed, and steamed.
yomari.suggested_accompaniments: Eaten warm when the inner chaku is delightfully molten.

chatpate.name: Chatpate
chatpate.description: Crisp, pungent, and explosive street snack tossed to order from puffed rice, dry Wai Wai instant noodles, boiled potatoes, chickpeas, raw onions, and freshly squeezed lemon juice.
chatpate.cultural_significance: Synonymous with school and college nostalgia, street corners, and lively gatherings.
chatpate.recipe_summary: All ingredients are rapidly hand-tossed inside a repurposed metal tin with a spoon and served in newspaper cones with bamboo picks.
chatpate.suggested_accompaniments: Enjoyed instantly on foot with friends!
